newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt market closes flat, losing strength.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt market closes flat, losing strength.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed lower most of Wednesday but higher U.S. yields reversed the early recovery in Europe and yields ended flat.
The main market focus was the U.S. unemployment figures due out on Friday.
"The Friday statistics are more and more in focus. I think the market will be sidelined and nervous until then. The uncertainty will continue to be priced in by higher yields," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates rose one basis point to 4.26 percent and ten-year bond yields were flat at 7.46 percent.
The crown softened to 4.5580 against the mark compared to 4.5420 late on Tuesday.
"It feels as if it's being related to the stock exchange. People are stepping away from any Scandinavian risks," one dealer said.
"All Scandinavian currencies are being sold mostly by foreigners," another dealer said.
